newsitem.title: ITALY: Clashes erupt at Bossi rally in Italy.
newsitem.headline: Clashes erupt at Bossi rally in Italy.

text.p: Police used tear gas after violence erupted following a rally by separatist leader Umberto Bossi in the northern Italian city of Turin on Friday night but a spokesman said matters were swiftly brought under control.
"The situation was always under control," the police spokesman said. "It looks like it's over now."

The spokesman said tear gas had been used to disperse some 700 ultra left-wing youths who approached a group of Bossi's Northern League party supporters attending a rally and fireworks show on the banks of the River Po.
The youths had pelted supporters with stones and glass and three or four police officers were slightly hurt as police moved in to break up the clash.
Several cars were also damaged, the spokesman said. He understood some civilians may also have been slightly injured but had no further details.

Bossi had held a rally in Turin at the end of the first leg of a three-day journey along the river, the longest in Italy, to publicise his quest for independence for a self-styled northern state he calls "Padania".
His journey is ends on Sunday in the lagoon city of Venice where he is due to declare "independence".
